params.why: third arc must be a sensible size

stem: Triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in a circle. The arc $BC$ (not containing $A$) measures ${=p}^\circ$ and $m(\angle C) = {=q}^\circ$. Find $m(\text{arc } AC)$ in degrees, the arc not containing $B$.
solution: $\angle C$ is subtended by arc $AB$, so $m(\text{arc } AB) = 2 \times {=q}^\circ = {=r}^\circ$.
The three arcs $AB$, $BC$, $AC$ make the whole circle, $360^\circ$.
notes: Mirrors book 14-2: double the inscribed angle to get its arc, then subtract from 360. Arc AB is the one opposite C.
